title: Promotion decision — controller variants A-G (schema-5 candidate control) vs rule-basis & Run3 schema-4

candidate.note: same schema-5 candidate model as the v5rank campaign; this campaign varies ONLY the score->utility control mapping (variants A-G), same bot source

bot.note: botSHA256 in the match reports is the digest of the EFFECTIVE source: the schema-5 model is embedded via SHADOW_V5_BUNDLED_MODEL before hashing for arms A-G, so those arms show eaf778bd...; rule-basis and run3-schema4 show the unmodified file hash f2b4c228... . The .user.js file itself is identical across all arms.

protocol: paired real-engine comparison, v5di seeds (disjoint from training/holdout namespaces), 3 modes x 2 maps x 2 opponents = 12 scenarios x 9 arms = 108 matches, 18000 ticks, Compact/Medium; observation unit = scenario (same seed isolates model/mapping effect)
promotionRule: A new champion must beat BOTH rule-basis AND Run3 schema-4 (plus safety + negative gates). Run3 stays ACTIVE until an explicit gated replacement. 'Verwerfe Varianten, die mehr Entscheidungen verändern, aber schlechter spielen' — reject variants that change more decisions but do not play better.

pairedVsRuleBasis.E: 5 pos / 6 neg / 1 zero (mean -2811.8; E == run3-schema4 in 12/12)

evidence.changedQuality: 95-99% of changed frames flip to a LOWER rule-utility candidate (0 up), avg utility loss 11.6-22.1, systematic bias toward 'naval' and 'invest'.
evidence.run3VsRuleBasis: run3-schema4 is below rule-basis on this dev set (mean -2811.8; 6 of 12 scenarios negative, 1 zero; confirmed W/L 3/7 vs 2/5)

negativeGates.safety: all arms preserve the full safety stack (legality authoritative downstream; failed frames fall back to the rule pick; no arm produced a fail-closed regression in land)
negativeGates.changedQuality: no arm's changed frames net positive rule utility (all net-negative or zero), so 'more changes' buys no utility
negativeGates.identity: A/B/C/D/F/G endLand is EXACTLY rule-basis endLand in 12/12 scenarios; E is EXACTLY run3-schema4 in 12/12

decision.reason: No controller variant (A-G) beats rule-basis: A/B/C/D/F/G are land-identical to rule-basis in all 12 scenarios (the candidate-control channel is provably neutral — the model re-ranks the bounded candidate list but the executed action, and thus land, never changes), and E is land-identical to run3-schema4 and below rule-basis. Per the rejection rule, the high-change arms (F 29%, C 15%, B 11%) buy zero land over the minimal-change arm A (2%). Since no variant beats rule-basis, none can beat BOTH rule-basis and Run3, so no gated replacement is triggered.
decision.verdict: Run3 schema-4 stays the ACTIVE champion. The schema-5 candidate-control channel (all five mapping variants) is retained as verified infrastructure (provenance, per-frame binding, safety preserved) but is NOT a champion this cycle. The two decisive levers for the next cycle are (1) the offline-to-live binding gap (the live gate admits ~2% of the model's offline-decided changes and the admitted changes are land-neutral) and (2) the model's systematic bias toward lower-utility 'naval'/'invest' candidates (§7 fine-tune condition is met).
